   170	`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/reviews/pr<N>/<sha>/`.  Nothing in the findings section
   171	is discarded either — a line that does not parse is kept verbatim as a
   172	`changes`-severity finding labelled `unparsed finding:`, and a non-approving
   173	verdict with an empty ledger gets one synthesised finding so the merge gate
   174	still blocks.  Both rules follow the same principle as rung 5: the failure mode
   175	worth engineering against is a review that reads green without having happened.
   176	
   177	## 7. Which reviews run
   178	
   179	* **Code review** always.  `pr-review.yml` ran it as a matrix over
   180	  `CLAUDE_CODE_REVIEW_PROVIDERS` (anthropic, deepseek).  Locally the matrix
   181	  collapses to one codex session; a second backend can be added by running
   182	  `review.sh` again with `MIPSTARRE_REVIEW_MODEL` set, which writes a separate
   183	  per-SHA file only if you also change the file name, so treat multi-provider
   184	  review as unimplemented rather than as a one-liner.
   185	* **Prose review** only when the diff touches `blueprint/`.  On GitHub it ran
   186	  unconditionally on a cheaper tier; gating it on the diff is a local
   187	  cost decision, not a weakening — the prose prompt reviews blueprint ↔ Lean
   188	  equivalence and blueprint prose, and a diff that touches no blueprint file
   189	  has nothing for it to review.  Set `MIPSTARRE_PROSE_MODEL` for the
   190	  cheaper-tier split.
   191	
   192	The failure semantics of the two are deliberately different, and the difference
   193	is inherited: `pr-review.yml:112-131` *fails* the code review when its token is
   194	missing, while `pr-review.yml:202-224` *skips* the prose review in the same
   195	situation.  Locally, a code reviewer that dies without output blocks the PR; a
   196	prose reviewer that dies leaves a warning and the code verdict stands.
   197	
   198	The published verdict takes the **worst** of the two lanes, written verbatim on
   199	the `VERDICT:` line of one exact-head `COMMENT` review (marker
   200	`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`): `APPROVED`, `COMMENTED` or
   201	`CHANGES_REQUESTED`.  Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT` too; adverseness lives
   202	in the paired `local-review/summary` status, `success` only for `APPROVED` or a
   203	`COMMENTED` verdict with an empty ledger and `failure` otherwise.  A head with
   204	no review at all simply has no such status, which the merge gate reads as
   205	"not reviewed" rather than as a pass.
   206	
   207	## 8. Concurrency
   208	
   209	| Lock | Key | Cancellation |
   210	|---|---|---|
   211	| review | PR id | none — a queued run waits, then re-checks the head |
   212	| fix (`autofix.md`) | branch | supersession sentinel |
   213	
   214	The split of keys is inherited (`pr-review.yml:18-20` groups by PR number with
   215	`cancel-in-progress: false`; `auto-fix.yml:259-261` groups by head branch with
   216	`cancel-in-progress: true`) and it matters: cancelling a review wastes the
   217	tokens already spent and produces nothing, whereas cancelling a superseded fix
   218	saves a write to a branch that has already moved.
   219	
   220	Locks are directories under `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/` holding the
   221	holder's pid — `flock(1)` does not exist on macOS.  A lock whose holder is gone

   223	tip and the remote PR head: a fix commit that landed while this run queued

   227	and forbids publication, leaving the raw output in the runtime cache.
   228	
   229	`review.sh` also refuses to start while a fix lock is held for the branch.
   230	The two tools share one worktree here, where GitHub gave each job a fresh
   231	checkout; without this cross-check the reviewer would read a tree being
   232	rewritten under it.
   233	
   234	## 9. The findings ledger
   235	
   236	`docs/pr_review_management.md` records the audit failure this replaces:
   237	review feedback lived on three separate GitHub surfaces — inline
   238	`pulls/N/comments`, issue-level `issues/N/comments`, and review summaries
   239	`pulls/N/reviews` — and PRs were merged with comments nobody had read.  The
   240	GraphQL `reviewThreads` `isResolved` / `isOutdated` pair was the only reliable
   241	status signal; the REST `line` field lied.
   242	
   243	Locally there is **one** surface.  Every finding lives on one line of the
   244	`## Findings` section of the exact-head `COMMENT` review body, between
   245	`<!-- findings:begin -->` and `<!-- findings:end -->`:
   246	
   247	    - [ ] F1 (blocker) `MIPStarRE/Basic.lean:120` — adds a non-paper hypothesis

   249	| Box | Meaning | Blocks merge |

   251	| `[ ]` | unresolved | **yes** |
   252	| `[x]` | resolved — a human or an agent addressed it and says so | no |
   253	| `[-]` | outdated — the cited lines were rewritten since the reviewed SHA | no |
   254	
   255	`[ ]` → `[x]` is a human judgement, or a claim by the fixer that a human is
   256	expected to check; it is never automatic.  There is no automatic `[ ]` → `[-]`
   257	pass: exactly one review is published per head SHA and the merge gate reads only
   258	that one, so a finding written against an older SHA can no longer block and has
   259	nothing to be outdated *out of*.  `[-]` stays available as a hand-written
   260	disposition; a reviewer re-derives its findings from the new diff on every head.

   273	
   274	Findings do **not** survive across SHAs.  Gate 4 matches the marker
   275	`<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->` on that exact commit id, so a ledger
   276	written at SHA *A* is invisible at SHA *B* — and a head carrying no review at

   279	
   280	A second review of the **same** SHA replaces that SHA's ledger, including any
   281	`[x]` a human had set.  `review.sh` copies the previous file into the run
   282	directory as `<name>.superseded` and warns when it did so, but it does not

   284	silently carrying resolutions across it would let a resolved-then-reintroduced
   285	finding disappear.  Resolve findings on the SHA you intend to keep.

   487	# rename(2) over an existing symlink.  `mv` is NOT usable here: BSD mv stat()s the
   488	# destination, follows the old `current` symlink to its directory, and would move
   489	# the new link *inside* the snapshot instead of replacing it.
   490	atomic_symlink() { # <target> <linkpath>
   491	  python3 - "$1" "$2" <<'PY'
   492	import os
   493	import sys
   494	
   495	target, link = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   496	tmp = "%s.tmp.%d" % (link, os.getpid())
   497	if os.path.islink(tmp) or os.path.exists(tmp):
   498	    os.remove(tmp)
   499	os.symlink(target, tmp)
   500	os.replace(tmp, link)
   501	PY
   502	}

   506	ensure_hot_repo() { # <primary-repo> <ref> -> prints the resolved sha
   507	  local primary="$1" ref="$2" sha="" candidate
   508	  mkdir -p "$HOT_MAIN"
   509	  if [ ! -d "$HOT_REPO/.git" ]; then
   510	    log "creating the hot main checkout at $HOT_REPO (clone of $primary)"
   511	    run_outside_git_env git clone --no-checkout "$primary" "$HOT_REPO" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
   512	      || die "failed to clone $primary into $HOT_REPO"
   513	  fi
   514	  run_outside_git_env git -C "$HOT_REPO" remote set-url origin "$primary" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
   515	  if ! run_outside_git_env git -C "$HOT_REPO" fetch --prune --tags origin >/dev/null 2>&1; then
   516	    warn "git fetch from $primary failed; using whatever the hot checkout already holds"
   517	  fi
   518	
   519	  if [ -n "$SHA" ]; then
   520	    sha="$(run_outside_git_env git -C "$HOT_REPO" rev-parse --verify "${SHA}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   521	    [ -n "$sha" ] || die "commit '$SHA' does not resolve in $HOT_REPO"
   522	  else
   523	    # DESIGN.md #8: origin/main must resolve.  Prefer it; accept a local branch.
   524	    for candidate in "origin/$ref" "$ref"; do
   525	      sha="$(run_outside_git_env git -C "$HOT_REPO" rev-parse --verify "${candidate}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   526	      [ -n "$sha" ] && break
   527	    done
   528	    [ -n "$sha" ] || die \
   529	      "neither origin/$ref nor $ref resolves in $HOT_REPO. If $primary has no commits yet, make the first commit on '$ref' before warming."
   530	  fi
   531	
   532	  # .lake/ is gitignored, so a forced checkout never touches the build tree, and
   533	  # `git clean` is deliberately not run (it would descend into vendored packages).
   534	  run_outside_git_env git -C "$HOT_REPO" checkout --detach --force "$sha" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
   535	    || die "failed to check out $sha in $HOT_REPO"
   536	  printf '%s' "$sha"
   537	}

   539	# The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround (docgen.yml:56-69).  `lake exe cache get`
   540	# runs `lake update`, whose mathlib post-update hook prunes
   541	# .lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib before fetching a cloud release; on a
   542	# tree that has never built, the directory does not exist and the uncaught
   543	# exception aborts the whole cache fetch.  Locally the same fetch also aborts when
   544	# a vendored package tree is *dirty* — build byproducts such as
   545	# widget/js/lake.trace block the revision checkout; see the 2026-08-30 failure and
   546	# its retry in results/telemetry/builds.jsonl.  Both are fresh-state bugs, and a
   547	# pristine checkout is exactly fresh state.
   548	proofwidgets_fresh_state_workaround() { # <tree>
   549	  local tree="$1" pkg name
   550	  [ -d "$tree/.lake/packages" ] || return 0
   551	  # Only tracked modifications are reset.  `git clean` is deliberately NOT run
   552	  # inside a vendored package: it would delete downloaded build output and cost
   553	  # hours to refetch.  If an untracked byproduct still blocks the checkout, the
   554	  # cache fetch fails loudly and the caller falls back to compiling from source.
   555	  for pkg in "$tree"/.lake/packages/*; do
   556	    [ -d "$pkg/.git" ] || continue
   557	    name="$(basename "$pkg")"
   558	    if [ -n "$(run_outside_git_env git -C "$pkg" status --porcelain --untracked-files=no 2>/dev/null || true)" ]; then
   559	      log "resetting dirty vendored package tree: $name"
   560	      run_outside_git_env git -C "$pkg" reset --hard >/dev/null 2>&1 \
   561	        || warn "could not reset $name; the Mathlib cache fetch may abort"
   562	    fi
   563	  done
   564	  if [ -d "$tree/.lake/packages/proofwidgets" ]; then
   565	    mkdir -p "$tree/.lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib"
   566	  fi
   567	}

   460	#
   461	# Ports housekeeping.yml:310-382: `lake exe cache get` then
   462	# `lake build -q --log-level=info`, teed to a log, summarized by
   463	# scripts/lean_linter_warning_report.py.  The upstream job explicitly did not
   464	# open a PR (housekeeping.yml:340-341) and neither does this one; any autofix
   465	# stays a separate, human-invoked command.
   466	#
   467	# The build takes the machine-wide advisory build lock required by
   468	# DESIGN.md:81-82 — one full `lake build` at a time — so a sweep cannot race an
   469	# agent's build or the cache warmer.
   470	
   471	job_linter_sweep() {
   472	  local reporter="${REPO_ROOT}/scripts/lean_linter_warning_report.py"
   473	  require_file "${reporter}" "the linter-warning parser ports unchanged"
   474	  command -v lake >/dev/null 2>&1 || die \
   475	    "lake is not on PATH; the linter sweep is a full Lean build and cannot run without it"
   476	
   477	  mkdir -p "${REPORT_DIR}" "${LOG_DIR}"
   478	  local log_file="${LOG_DIR}/lean-build-$(timestamp).log"
   479	
   480	  note "linter-sweep: full lake build under the machine-wide build lock (this is slow)"
   481	  # THE machine-wide full-build mutex — same path and mkdir protocol as
   482	  # cache-warmer.sh, warm-worktree.sh and ci.sh (DESIGN.md invariant 7).
   483	  # A live owner is never broken; a dead owner's lock is.
   484	  local build_lock="${MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK:-${CACHE_ROOT}/.full-build-lock}"
   485	  local waited=0 wait_max="${MIPSTARRE_CI_BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S:-14400}"
   486	  while ! mkdir "${build_lock}" 2>/dev/null; do
   487	    local owner_pid
   488	    owner_pid="$(head -n 1 "${build_lock}/owner" 2>/dev/null || true)"
   489	    if [ -n "${owner_pid}" ] && kill -0 "${owner_pid}" 2>/dev/null; then
   490	      [ "${waited}" -ge "${wait_max}" ] && die \
   491	        "could not take ${build_lock} within ${wait_max}s (held by pid ${owner_pid})"
   492	      [ "${waited}" -eq 0 ] && note "waiting for build lock ${build_lock} (pid ${owner_pid})"
   493	      sleep 15; waited=$((waited + 15))
   494	    else
   495	      note "breaking stale build lock ${build_lock} (owner dead or unreadable)"
   496	      rm -rf "${build_lock}"
   497	    fi
   498	  done
   499	  printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$$" "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "housekeeping linter-sweep" \
   500	    > "${build_lock}/owner"
   501	  # shellcheck disable=SC2064  # expand build_lock now, not at trap time
   502	  trap "rm -rf '${build_lock}'" RETURN
   503	  run_locked "${LOCK_DIR}/lake-build.lock" \
   504	    "${SCRIPT_DIR}/housekeeping.sh" --internal-lean-build "${log_file}"
   505	
   506	  note "linter-sweep: summarizing warnings"
   507	  python3 "${reporter}" \
   508	    --log "${log_file}" \
   509	    --json "${REPORT_DIR}/lean-linter-warnings.json" \
   510	    --text "${REPORT_DIR}/lean-linter-warnings.txt"
   511	  note "linter-sweep: build log ${log_file}"
   512	  note "linter-sweep: reports in ${REPORT_DIR}/lean-linter-warnings.{json,txt}"
   513	}

   341	* **Metadata layout.** `ci.sh` records its holder in `<lock>/owner` (pid, ISO
   342	  time, tag — one per line); these scripts record `<lock>/info` as `key=value`.
   343	  A script that cannot read the other's holder would conclude "no pid, therefore
   344	  stale" and break a *live* lock mid-build. Therefore: every acquisition here
   345	  writes **both** files, and staleness detection reads `info` first, then
   346	  `owner`, and falls back to the lock directory's mtime for age. An absent `host`
   347	  field is read as "this host", which keeps pid liveness authoritative.

   381	### 8.1 Git environment hygiene
   382	
   383	Every invocation of `lake` or of `git` inside a vendored package is wrapped in
   384	`run_outside_git_env`, ported from `.githooks/pre-push:19-25`: it unsets every
   385	variable named by `git rev-parse --local-env-vars` in a subshell. Without it, a
   386	script invoked from inside a git hook leaks `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_INDEX_FILE` into
   387	Lake's package checkouts, and nested git operations resolve the wrong repository.
   388	
   389	### 8.2 The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround
   390	
   391	Kept verbatim in intent from `docgen.yml:56-69`, in all three scripts, because a
   392	pristine agent worktree is exactly the fresh state that triggers it.
   393	
   394	*Upstream form.* `lake exe cache get` runs `lake update`, whose mathlib
   395	post-update hook prunes `.lake/packages/proofwidgets/.lake/build/lib` before
   396	fetching a cloud release. On a tree that has never built, the directory does not
   397	exist, and the uncaught exception aborts the **entire** cache fetch. Fix: create
   398	the directory, but only if `proofwidgets` was actually checked out.
   399	
   400	*Local form.* The same fetch also aborts when a vendored package tree is
   401	**dirty**: build byproducts (`widget/js/lake.trace`) block the revision checkout.
   402	Recorded in `results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, 2026-08-30 — a failed build followed
   403	by a successful retry after `git reset --hard` in the package. The scripts
   404	therefore reset any vendored package tree with **tracked** modifications before
   405	fetching.
   406	
   407	`git clean` is deliberately **not** run inside a vendored package: it would delete
   408	downloaded build output at a cost of hours. If an untracked byproduct still blocks
   409	a checkout, the fetch fails loudly and the caller falls back to compiling from
   410	source.

   414	## 9. Telemetry
   415	
   416	Every full build and every cache event appends one JSON line to
   417	`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`, per `DESIGN.md`'s telemetry contract.
   418	
   419	```jsonc
   420	{"ts": "<ISO 8601 with offset>",
   421	 "kind": "warm" | "rebuild" | "cache-get",
   422	 "trigger": "<who asked for this>",
   423	 "outcome": "success" | "failed",
   424	 "seconds": <int>,
   425	 "sha": "<commit, when known>",
   426	 "note": "<sanitized, ≤400 chars>"}
   427	```
   428	
   429	* `warm` — a warmer build and publish.
   430	* `rebuild` — a consumer's full `lake build` (cold path, or `--build`).
   431	* `cache-get` — a per-worktree tier-2 fetch.
   432	
   433	Three properties are load-bearing:
   434	
   435	* **The primary checkout owns the file.** Even when invoked from a linked
   436	  worktree, the scripts resolve `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` back to the
   437	  primary repository, so an append-only JSONL does not fork per worktree and
   438	  produce merge conflicts. Override with `MIPSTARRE_TELEMETRY_DIR`.
   439	* **Appends are serialized** by a short-lived `mkdir` lock, and give up after 5 s
   440	  rather than delaying a build. Telemetry never blocks or fails a build; every
   441	  failure path degrades to a warning.
   442	* **`note` is sanitized** — non-printable characters stripped, truncated to 400
   443	  characters — because notes may quote build output, and compiler output is
   444	  untrusted text regardless of where it was produced (`DESIGN.md` #6).

   449	
   450	```bash
   451	# Seed or refresh the hot main cache (do this after every merge to main).
   452	local/bin/cache-warmer.sh --ref main
   453	
   454	# What is published right now?
   455	local/bin/cache-warmer.sh --status
   456	
   457	# Bootstrap a brand-new agent worktree end to end.
   458	local/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/.worktrees/issue-0042-qpbt-basis
   459	
   460	# Verify an existing worktree without touching it.
   461	local/bin/worktree-setup.sh /path/to/worktree --check
   462	
   463	# Re-warm a worktree after the warmer published a newer snapshot.
   464	local/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --force
   465	
   466	# What would this worktree do, warm or cold?
   467	local/bin/warm-worktree.sh /path/to/worktree --status
   468	```
   469	
   470	After a toolchain or Mathlib bump lands on `main`, the ordering is fixed: **warm
   471	first, adopt second.** The bump changes the keyhash, so every existing snapshot
   472	is invalid and every worktree cold-paths until a fresh snapshot exists. Run
   473	`cache-warmer.sh --ref main` before dispatching agents, or pay for a full build in
   474	each worktree serialized behind one lock.

   478	## 11. Failure modes and how each degrades
   479	
   480	| condition | behaviour |
   481	|---|---|
   482	| No snapshot published yet | Warn, name the warmer command, take the cold path. |
   483	| Keyhash mismatch | Warn with both hashes, take the cold path. Never a partial reuse. |
   484	| Malformed / unreadable `STAMP` | Treated as *no snapshot*; cold path. |
   485	| Snapshot is `partial` | Used, with a warning naming the SHA that failed. |
   486	| `cp -c` unsupported (non-APFS, cross-volume) | Warn, fall back to `cp -R`. Correct, just slower and larger. |
   487	| `lake exe cache get` fails | Warn; tier 2 gets compiled from source. Non-fatal. |
   488	| Full-build lock held | Wait; the warmer waits indefinitely by default, consumers time out per `--lock-timeout`. |
   489	| Stale lock (dead pid, or age > TTL) | Broken by atomic rename, with a warning naming the dead holder. |
   490	| Primary repo has no commits on `main` | Hard error naming the cause. Never a silent no-op. |
   491	| `warm-worktree.sh` missing during bootstrap | Hard error. `--skip-warm` is the explicit opt-out. |
   492	| `origin/main` does not resolve | Warning, non-zero exit from `--check`, because hooks self-disable silently. |
   493	| `python3` absent | Warmer: hard error (needed for the atomic publish). Consumer: warning, telemetry skipped. |

     6	## Standing principles
     7	
     8	1. **Protocols are normative until amended.** An agent that finds a protocol
     9	   wrong, ambiguous, or costly does not silently deviate: it follows the
    10	   protocol (or stops), records the friction in
    11	   `results/telemetry/events.md`, and proposes an amendment — a dispatched
    12	   worker proposes it to the operator; the operator amends directly under the
    13	   procedure below, an `events.md` incident being a sufficient trigger.  Owner
    14	   sign-off is needed only for the escalations named in the standing briefing.
    15	2. **Amendments are evidence-driven.** Every change to a file under
    16	   `local/protocols/` or to `AGENTS.md` must append an entry to

1	# Build cache protocol — the hot main cache
     2	
     3	Normative. This document specifies the local replacement for the parent
     4	workflow's GitHub Actions build cache, and the rules every worktree must obey to
     5	avoid duplicate compilation. It is the protocol behind three executables:
     6	
     7	| script | role |
     8	|---|---|
     9	| `local/bin/cache-warmer.sh` | the **single writer**: builds `main`, publishes read-only snapshots |
    10	| `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh` | the **consumer**: keyhash-gated copy-on-write clone into a worktree |
    11	| `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` | fresh-worktree bootstrap (replaces `.codex/setup.sh`) |
    12	
    13	Governing invariants: `local/DESIGN.md` #1 (single cache writer) and #7 (one full
    14	`lake build` machine-wide). Where this document and `DESIGN.md` disagree,
    15	`DESIGN.md` wins.
    16	
    17	---
    18	
    19	## 1. What is being replaced, and why it was built that way
    20	
    21	The parent repository's caching design is the residue of a specific, documented
    22	failure. The load-bearing citations:
    23	
    24	| parent mechanism | citation | what it encodes |
    25	|---|---|---|
    26	| Split restore/save, save only on `main` | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:137-167` | *"The cache is saved only from main and restored everywhere."* |
    27	| `lean-action`'s own cache disabled | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:138-142` | The post-mortem: a ~2.6 GB entry saved **per PR run** cycled through the 10 GB repository cache budget and evicted the main-branch entry, *"so no run ever restored usable MIPStarRE oleans and every run rebuilt the whole library."* |
    28	| Same policy restated in the weekly job | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:75-77` | *"See pr-ci.yml: per-run lake caches evict the main build cache from the repository cache budget."* |
    29	| Main runs exempt from cancellation | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:50` | *"Do not cancel main-branch runs: they seed the build cache."* |
    30	| Save runs `if: always()` on main | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:161-162` | *"Save even when the build failed: a partial cache still spares the next run the modules that did compile."* |
    31	| ProofWidgets prune workaround | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:56-69` | A fresh-tree upstream bug that aborts the entire Mathlib cache fetch |
    32	| `elan` install isolated from the cache lifecycle | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:44-54` | Avoids *"a partial cache save or restore-then-overwrite that could negate the ProofWidgets workaround"* |
    33	| Independent cache for the doc subproject | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:135-140` | `docbuild/` is its own Lake project with its own key |
    34	| Mathlib bumps are manual only | `.github/workflows/update.yml:3-5` | A bump *"triggers a full library rebuild and possibly an auto-fix cascade"* |
    35	| Lean setup removed from a PR job | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:314` | A job was demoted to a notice *"after repeated runner disk exhaustion"* |
    36	
    37	The single sentence to carry forward: **many writers destroyed the one valuable
    38	cache entry.** Every rule below exists to make that impossible locally, where the
    39	same failure mode reappears as parallel agent worktrees writing into a shared
    40	build tree.
    41	
    42	---
    43	
    44	## 2. The two-tier split
    45	
    46	`.lake/` holds two caches with different provenance, different lifetimes, and
    47	different sharing rules. Conflating them is the primary way to reintroduce the
    48	parent's failure.
    49	
    50	**Tier 1 — `.lake/build`** — this project's own compiled artifacts (`.olean`,
    51	`.ilean`, `.c`, `.trace` for `MIPStarRE` modules). This is *exactly* what the
    52	parent cached, and only from `main`. Locally it is produced by the warmer and
    53	distributed as copy-on-write clones. Each worktree owns a **private, writable**
    54	copy.
    55	
    56	**Tier 2 — `.lake/packages`** — Mathlib and its transitive dependencies. The
    57	parent never put these in the GitHub cache; they come from Mathlib's own cloud
    58	cache via `lake exe cache get` inside `lean-action`. Locally they live **once
    59	per manifest** in a shared, read-only store:
    60	`$CACHE_ROOT/packages/<key>`, `key = sha256(lake-manifest.json ‖ lean-toolchain)[:16]`,
    61	and every worktree's `.lake/packages` is a symlink to it.
    62	
    63	> **Why a shared store is safe here (2026-09-03).** The old objection — a
    64	> shared tree is read-only only by convention, so one `lake update` mutates it
    65	> for everyone — is answered mechanically: the store is `chmod -R a-w`, so any
    66	> write (an automated `lake update`, a dependency rebuild after a manifest
    67	> drift) fails loudly in the one worktree that attempted it. Identity is by
    68	> key, so a Mathlib bump simply creates a new store entry; worktrees on the old
    69	> manifest keep linking the old one. The first worktree to need a key fetches
    70	> with `lake exe cache get` into a real directory, then *publishes* it (move,
    71	> `chmod a-w`, link); later worktrees only link. Cost: 7.3 GB once per key
    72	> instead of per worktree (8 copies = 58 GB on 2026-09-03, on a 97 % full disk).
    73	> `worktree-setup.sh` still refuses to run `lake update`.
    74	
    75	Consequence for `lake update`: it is not part of any automated path here. It
    76	rewrites `lake-manifest.json`, which moves the cache key (§3) out from under
    77	every published snapshot, and it mutates vendored package checkouts. Mathlib
    78	bumps stay human-invoked, exactly as `update.yml:3-5` argues.
    79	
    80	---
    81	
    82	## 3. The cache key
    83	
    84	```
    85	keyhash := sha256( bytes(lean-toolchain) ‖ bytes(lake-manifest.json) ‖ bytes(lakefile.toml) )
    86	```
    87	
    88	concatenated in that fixed order, `‖` being byte concatenation. This is the local
    89	analog of `hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lake-manifest.json', 'lakefile.toml')` in
    90	`pr-ci.yml:143-149`. The definition is duplicated verbatim in `cache-warmer.sh`
    91	and `warm-worktree.sh` (function `compute_keyhash`); the two copies **must stay
    92	byte-identical**, or every consumer silently and permanently takes the cold path.
    93	A missing input file is a hard error, never a default.
    94	
    95	Two properties matter, and they are not symmetric:
    96	
    97	1. **A snapshot may be older than the consumer's base commit.** The parent's
    98	   `restore-keys` deliberately drop the SHA suffix and prefix-match the newest
    99	   entry under the same hash. This is safe because Lake's staleness test is
   100	   trace-hash based, not mtime based: a cloned artifact whose inputs still hash
   101	   equal is reused, and everything else is rebuilt. Cloned files therefore do not
   102	   need their timestamps preserved.
   103	2. **A snapshot must never cross a keyhash boundary.** A `lean-toolchain` bump,
   104	   a Mathlib revision change, or a `lakefile.toml` edit is *total* invalidation.
   105	   `warm-worktree.sh` compares its own keyhash against the snapshot `STAMP`
   106	   before copying anything, and on mismatch refuses the clone, warns, and falls
   107	   back to the cold path. It never partially reuses.
   108	
   109	---
   110	
   111	## 4. On-disk layout
   112	
   113	All runtime state lives under `MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT`, default
   114	`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/`. Nothing in this tree is ever committed.
   115	
   116	```
   117	~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/
   118	├── .full-build-lock/            # machine-wide: one full `lake build` at a time
   119	│   └── info                     # pid, host, started, started_epoch, purpose
   120	├── .telemetry-lock/             # short-lived; serializes JSONL appends
   121	├── logs/                        # captured build logs (warm-*.log, worktree-build-*.log)
   122	└── hot-main/
   123	    ├── .writer-lease/           # only the warmer holds this
   124	    │   └── info
   125	    ├── repo/                    # the always-warm detached checkout of main
   126	    ├── snapshots/
   127	    │   ├── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/
   128	    │   │   ├── STAMP
   129	    │   │   └── build/           # a byte copy of repo/.lake/build
   130	    │   └── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/
   131	    └── current -> snapshots/snap-<utc>-<sha12>   # absolute symlink
   132	```
   133	
   134	Snapshot names are `snap-<YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ>-<sha12>` so that reverse
   135	lexicographic order *is* reverse chronological order — the GC needs no `stat`
   136	calls and no name parsing.
   137	
   138	### `STAMP` schema
   139	
   140	A flat `key=value` file, one pair per line. It is **data, not code**: both scripts
   141	parse it with a whitelist and validate each value (`keyhash` must be 64 lowercase
   142	hex characters, `status ∈ {complete, partial}`, `sha` hex). Nothing in it is ever
   143	`eval`ed or `source`d.
   144	
   145	```
   146	sha=<full 40-char commit sha of the build>
   147	keyhash=<64 hex chars, §3>
   148	timestamp=<ISO 8601 with offset>
   149	timestamp_epoch=<unix seconds>
   150	status=complete|partial
   151	build_seconds=<integer>
   152	toolchain=<contents of lean-toolchain>
   153	snapshot=<snapshot directory name>
   154	warmer_version=1
   155	```
   156	
   157	---
   158	
   159	## 5. The warmer — `cache-warmer.sh`
   160	
   161	```
   162	local/bin/cache-warmer.sh [--ref main | --sha <sha>] [--force] [--keep N]
   163	                          [--targets "<lake targets>"] [--lock-timeout S]
   164	                          [--lease-ttl S] [--gc-only] [--status]
   165	```
   166	
   167	### 5.1 Writer lease
   168	
   169	Acquired by `mkdir hot-main/.writer-lease` — `mkdir(2)` is the atomic
   170	test-and-set. The lease directory holds an `info` file with `pid`, `host`,
   171	`started`, `started_epoch`, `purpose`.
   172	
   173	Staleness is decided in this order:
   174	
   175	* **Same host**: the holder's liveness is authoritative (`kill -0 pid`). A dead
   176	  pid means stale immediately; a live pid means *not* stale regardless of age.
   177	* **Different host, or no pid**: fall back to age > TTL (default 43200 s).
   178	
   179	The TTL is deliberately much larger than the study map's suggested 3 h: this
   180	repository's own cold full build took **25052 s** (`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`,
   181	2026-08-30). An age-only rule with a short TTL would break a live warmer's lease
   182	mid-build and produce exactly the concurrent-writer situation the lease exists to
   183	prevent.
   184	
   185	**Breaking a stale lock is done by renaming, not deleting.** Two processes that
   186	both judge a lock stale will both attempt `mv lockdir lockdir.stale.<pid>.<epoch>`;
   187	`rename(2)` is atomic, so exactly one succeeds and proceeds to delete and
   188	re-acquire, while the loser loops and finds the lock freshly held. A
   189	`rm -rf && mkdir` sequence has no such guarantee.
   190	
   191	### 5.2 Build
   192	
   193	1. Clone or fetch `hot-main/repo` from the primary checkout; resolve `origin/<ref>`
   194	   first, then `<ref>` (`DESIGN.md` #8). Check out **detached** and forced.
   195	   `.lake/` is gitignored, so the checkout never touches the build tree, and
   196	   `git clean` is deliberately not run (it would descend into vendored packages).
   197	2. Apply the fresh-state workaround (§8.2).
   198	3. Acquire the machine-wide full-build lock (§7) — **waiting, never aborting.**
   199	   This is the local reading of `pr-ci.yml:50`: a main build seeds the cache and
   200	   is never cancelled in favour of a newer commit. If main moves during a build,
   201	   finish, then warm again.
   202	4. `lake exe cache get` (failure is a warning, not fatal — the build simply
   203	   compiles more from source), then `lake build`, then any `--targets`.
   204	   **No `lake update`.**
   205	5. Everything is logged to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/logs/warm-<utc>-<sha12>.log`.
   206	   Telemetry records the log *path*, never log *content* — build output is
   207	   untrusted text (`DESIGN.md` #6) and does not belong in a data file that agent
   208	   prompts may later read.
   209	
   210	### 5.3 Atomic publish
   211	
   212	The publish sequence, and the reason each step is in this order:
   213	
   214	1. Copy `repo/.lake/build` into `snapshots/<name>.tmp/build` with
   215	   `cp -c -R` (APFS copy-on-write; falls back to `cp -R` with a warning if the
   216	   source and destination are not on the same APFS volume).
   217	2. Write `snapshots/<name>.tmp/STAMP`.
   218	3. `mv snapshots/<name>.tmp snapshots/<name>` — a same-directory `rename(2)`.
   219	   A snapshot directory therefore becomes visible only when it is already
   220	   complete and stamped. **A reader can never observe a torn snapshot.**
   221	4. Re-point `current` by creating a sibling symlink and `os.replace`-ing it over
   222	   the old one (`rename(2)` again, which does not follow symlinks).
   223	
   224	> Step 4 is done through `python3`, not `mv`. BSD `mv` `stat()`s its destination,
   225	> follows the existing `current` symlink to the directory it names, and would
   226	> move the new link *inside* the snapshot instead of replacing it. This is a real
   227	> trap, not a hypothetical one.
   228	
   229	Consumers exploit exactly this: they `readlink current` **once**, and hold the
   230	resolved concrete path for the rest of the run.
   231	
   232	### 5.4 Partial snapshots are intentional
   233	
   234	If `lake build` fails, the warmer still publishes, with `status=partial`, and
   235	exits non-zero. This is `pr-ci.yml:161-162` ported directly: a broken `main`
   236	commit must not stall every consumer at zero cache, and the modules that did
   237	compile are still worth distributing. Consumers accept partial snapshots and say
   238	so loudly.
   239	
   240	A non-zero exit from the warmer therefore means *"main did not build cleanly"* —
   241	not *"nothing was published."* A cron wrapper should treat it as an alert, not a
   242	reason to retry.
   243	
   244	### 5.5 Retention
   245	
   246	Keep the newest `--keep` snapshots (default 2), the local analog of the parent's
   247	10 GB repository cache budget. **The snapshot `current` points to is never
   248	collected**, even when it falls outside the keep window: a consumer that has
   249	resolved `current` must find a live directory. Abandoned `*.tmp` staging

   354	snapshot_list_newest_first() {
   355	  # Snapshot names are snap-<utc-timestamp>-<sha12>, so a reverse lexicographic
   356	  # sort is a reverse chronological sort.
   357	  [ -d "$SNAPSHOTS" ] || return 0
   358	  find "$SNAPSHOTS" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'snap-*' 2>/dev/null \
   359	    | sed 's|.*/||' | grep -v '\.tmp$' | LC_ALL=C sort -r || true
   360	}

   362	current_target() {
   363	  [ -L "$CURRENT_LINK" ] || return 1
   364	  local target
   365	  target="$(readlink "$CURRENT_LINK")" || return 1
   366	  [ -n "$target" ] || return 1
   367	  [ -d "$target" ] || return 1
   368	  printf '%s' "$target"
   369	}
   370	
   371	stamp_field() { # <stamp-file> <key>
   372	  local file="$1" key="$2" line value
   373	  [ -f "$file" ] || return 1
   374	  while IFS= read -r line; do
   375	    case "$line" in
   376	      "$key="*)
   377	        value="${line#*=}"
   378	        # STAMP is on-disk data, not code: validate, never eval or source.
   379	        case "$key" in
   380	          keyhash)
   381	            [ "${#value}" -eq 64 ] || return 1
   382	            case "$value" in *[!0-9a-f]*) return 1 ;; esac
   383	            ;;
   384	          sha)
   385	            case "$value" in ''|*[!0-9a-f]*) return 1 ;; esac
   386	            ;;
   387	          status)
   388	            case "$value" in complete|partial) ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
   389	            ;;
   390	        esac
   391	        printf '%s' "$value"
   392	        return 0
   393	        ;;
   394	    esac
   395	  done < "$file"
   396	  return 1
   397	}

   420	gc_snapshots() {
   421	  local keep="$KEEP" kept=0 name protected path
   422	  if [ "$keep" -lt 1 ]; then
   423	    keep=1
   424	  fi
   425	  protected="$(current_target || true)"

   429	    kept=$((kept + 1))

   432	    fi

   434	    # keep window: consumers resolve `current` once and must find a live tree.
   435	    if [ -n "$protected" ] && [ "$path" = "$protected" ]; then
   436	      log "GC keeping $name: it is the published 'current' snapshot"
   437	      continue
   438	    fi
   439	    log "GC removing snapshot $name"
   440	    rm -rf "$path"
   441	  done <<< "$(snapshot_list_newest_first)"
   442	  find "$SNAPSHOTS" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'snap-*.tmp' -mmin +60 \
   443	    -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null || true
   444	}

   521	## 13. Invariant checklist
   522	
   523	A change to any of these scripts must preserve all of the following:
   524	
   525	1. Only `cache-warmer.sh` writes into `hot-main/`. Consumers refuse to run there.
   526	2. `compute_keyhash` is byte-identical across both scripts.
   527	3. A snapshot becomes visible only via `rename(2)`, fully built and stamped.
   528	4. `current` is re-pointed only via `rename(2)` over the symlink — never `mv`.
   529	5. Consumers resolve `current` exactly once per run.
   530	6. Keyhash mismatch → cold path. Never a partial or best-effort reuse.
   531	7. Failed builds still publish, flagged `partial`.
   532	8. GC never removes the snapshot `current` names.
   533	9. At most one full `lake build` machine-wide; `lake env lean` takes no lock.
   534	10. `.lake/packages` is a symlink to the read-only store `$CACHE_ROOT/packages/<key>`;
   535	    the store is `chmod a-w`; no automated `lake update`.
   536	11. The ProofWidgets fresh-state workaround runs before any `lake exe cache get`.
   537	12. Every `lake` / vendored-`git` invocation goes through `run_outside_git_env`.
   538	13. `STAMP` is parsed by whitelist and validated; never `eval`ed or `source`d.
   539	14. Telemetry is best-effort, serialized, sanitized, and lands in the primary checkout.
   540	15. Every degradation is a loud warning or a hard error. Never a silent no-op.

## Findings

- [ ] F1 (blocker) `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh:502` — Concurrent publication can strand the loser without packages while reporting success.
- [ ] F2 (blocker) `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh:502` — Dependencies become read-only before cache misses can be compiled.
- [ ] F3 (blocker) `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh:480` — Store readiness accepts dangling, unverified, or private package trees as success.
- [ ] F4 (blocker) `local/bin/cache-warmer.sh:691` — The warmer accepts any package symlink without validating its manifest key.
- [ ] F5 (blocker) `local/bin/ci.sh:825` — CI can build a manifest-changing PR against a stale package-store symlink.
- [ ] F6 (blocker) `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh:173` — Bootstrap follows package symlinks before validation and can reset an external checkout.
- [ ] F7 (blocker) `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh:215` — The shared build lock is exposed before ownership metadata and can be stolen.
- [ ] F8 (changes) `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh:258` — `INT` or `TERM` can be converted into a successful exit.
- [ ] F9 (changes) `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh:473` — Store key generation bypasses the portable SHA-256 helper.
- [ ] F10 (changes) `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh:502` — First publication fails across filesystems because it relies on `mv -T`.
- [ ] F11 (changes) `local/bin/housekeeping.sh:522` — The linter sweep writes through the read-only link and masks resulting failures.
- [ ] F12 (blocker) `local/protocols/EVOLUTION.md:414` — The protocol amendment lacks the incident or telemetry citation required by `meta.md`.
- [ ] F13 (changes) `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh:31` — Operator and script documentation still describes tier 2 as private and never symlinked.
- [ ] F14 (changes) `-` — No behavioral regression test covers publication, validation, migration, permissions, or caller integration.

## Review

The implementation remains the original 98-line change; none of the substantive repairs described by the prior ledger is present.

For F1, two publishers can both move their private trees into distinct incoming paths. The losing final `mv` fails after its source is gone, while line 525 discards the failure and returns success. Interrupted incoming trees are likewise never reclaimed.

For F2, successful `cache get` is not proof that every dependency artifact exists. Freezing the tree before `lake build` prevents the documented cache-miss fallback from compiling missing artifacts.

For F3, an expected but dangling symlink returns success without checking its target. Any directory at the keyed path is accepted without completeness or permission validation, and populated legacy copies are deliberately left private while still returning success.

F4 and F5 break the key boundary. The hot warmer skips every symlink, and CI only invokes `warm-worktree.sh` when `.lake/build` is absent. A manifest change can therefore use old dependencies and publish or validate artifacts under the new key. The warmer also captures its key before `cache get`, despite documenting that this command can update the manifest.

For F6, setup runs `git reset --hard` and `mkdir` through `.lake/packages` before the warmer validates or replaces the link. A malformed top-level or nested link can target unrelated writable data.

For F7, `mkdir` publishes the mutex before `owner` exists. Housekeeping treats that window as stale and removes it, allowing two full builds; later unconditional removal can also release another process’s lock.

F8 was reproduced directly: the current cleanup pattern exits with status `0` when `TERM` arrives after a successful command.

F9 and F10 violate the existing macOS and cross-volume contract: the new code uses `sha256sum` instead of `sha256_stdin`, and GNU-only, same-filesystem `mv -T`.

F11 conflicts with the claimed live migration of the primary checkout. Its unconditional `lake exe cache get` writes through the shared link, while the surrounding pipeline converts package or build failure into success.

F12 does not satisfy `meta.md:37-42`: “owner audit” is not a durable citation to the required dated event or telemetry line.

F13 includes the stale header here, the per-worktree cache-fetch language still present in `build-cache.md`, and the direct `lake exe cache get` quick start in `AGENTS.md`.

The repeated prior findings consolidate into F1-F14. The prior test-lock and trusted-path findings referred to files absent from this patch; the cache-fetch-then-build concern is not separate because the current protocol explicitly permits source compilation. Shell syntax and `git diff --check` pass, but F14 explains why green CI does not validate this feature.

The four-round cap has been reached. Under `review.md` §12, there should be no sixth general review round: every finding above must be fixed or assigned a tracked issue and disposed in an exact-head `ADJUDICATION` comment. No issue dispositions were supplied here.
